rules.title: Multiple severe indicators in one file
rules.description: Three or more high-severity indicators in a single file is a compound signal: individually each might be a heuristic artifact, together they describe a capability.
rules.remediation: Treat the file as hostile until reviewed. Do not execute it; collect the hash and submit it for deeper analysis.

rules.title: SSH hardening gaps combine into exposure
rules.description: Several failed SSH controls at once usually means the daemon is at its distribution default, which permits root login and password authentication.
rules.remediation: Apply the SSH baseline as one change set: no root login, key-only authentication, bounded attempts, no empty passwords.

rules.title: Content findings and host misconfiguration agree
rules.description: A file indicator was found while the host audit also reports real failures. A weak host makes a content indicator materially more dangerous.
rules.remediation: Fix the host findings first, then review the file that matched. Containment is cheaper than cleanup.

rules.title: Two independent content engines agree
rules.description: YARA and the native indicator engine both fired on the same file. Independent detection paths agreeing raises confidence substantially.
rules.remediation: Prioritise this file in triage; two engines agreeing is stronger evidence than either alone.

rules.title: Widespread medium-severity findings
rules.description: Six or more medium findings across a scan suggests systemic weakness rather than a single mistake.
rules.remediation: Group the findings by category and fix the largest cluster first; systemic issues usually share one root cause.

rules.title: Credential material beside an exfiltration channel
rules.description: Credential indicators and an outbound data channel in the same scan is the shape of a harvesting script, not an accident.
rules.remediation: Rotate every credential the scan could reach, block the destination, and review process history on the host.

rules.title: Persistence paired with privilege escalation
rules.description: A persistence mechanism plus an escalation primitive is a complete foothold: it survives reboot and can gain root.
rules.remediation: Remove the persistence entry and the escalation path together; removing one alone leaves the other active.

rules.title: Audit trail tampering indicators
rules.description: Anti-forensic actions were detected. Evidence collection must happen before any cleanup.
rules.remediation: Preserve centralised logs and memory before remediation; local logs may already be unreliable.
